biography: Francisco 'Chico' Serra burst onto the Brazilian racing scene with a raw, untamed aggression that quickly turned heads. Hailing from a modest background in São Paulo, Chico’s first taste of speed came from illicit street races in his father’s beat-up Uno. It wasn't long before he caught the eye of a local Copa Uno team manager during one of these impromptu events. His debut season was a whirlwind of spectacular crashes and breathtaking overtakes, a chaotic ballet that both thrilled and terrified spectators. After a brief stint with Rich Racing, marked by a near-miss championship win marred by a controversial penalty in the final race, Chico moved to Molas Hoesch, hoping for a more structured environment. Currently, he's finding his feet with WB Motorsport, aiming to refine his natural talent and transform his raw speed into consistent podium finishes. While his youthful exuberance sometimes gets the better of him, there's no denying the fire in Chico's belly and the potential for greatness that lies within.
drivingStyle: Chico's driving style is best described as relentlessly aggressive. He attacks every corner with a late-braking, high-risk approach, often pushing the limits of his car and the track. While his tire management is a work in progress, his ability to maintain composure under pressure is surprisingly strong. Chico thrives in wheel-to-wheel combat, relishing the opportunity to make daring overtakes. He has a knack for sensing opportunities and exploiting the smallest gaps, often leaving his rivals in disbelief.

rivalries.name: Ricardo 'The Professor' Vargas
rivalries.reason: A clash of styles; Vargas, a seasoned veteran known for his smooth, calculated driving, constantly clashes with Chico's impulsive, high-risk approach.

rivalries.name: Isabela 'Ice Queen' Fonseca
rivalries.reason: Fonseca, a rising star known for her ice-cold focus, sees Chico as a reckless upstart undermining the integrity of the sport.

rivalries.name: Paulo 'The Hammer' Costa
rivalries.reason: Both drivers have similar aggressive styles, resulting in several on-track collisions and a heated exchange of words after a particularly contentious race at Interlagos.

quirks: Always wears a lucky wristband his grandmother gave him before every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song to calm his nerves before getting into the car.
Has a habit of cleaning his visor obsessively, even when it's already spotless.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, or I'm going home in pieces!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Copa Uno championship race at Interlagos in his rookie year, overtaking three cars in the final lap with a daring move that cemented his reputation as a fearless competitor.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Rich Racing championship decider due to excessive tire wear, costing him the title and leading to accusations of recklessness.
